title: The Silent Fungal Pandemic (Candida auris & Mucorales) & First-in-Class Antifungals in 20 Years: Amphotericin B, CYP51, FKS1, Olorofim & Fosmanogepix — One-Ångström walks inside Candida CYP51 + tetrazole VT-1161 (5TZ1), fungal CYP51 + fluconazole revealing the Tyr132/Tyr140 Y132F water-bridge collapse (4WMZ), cryo-EM 1,3-β-glucan synthase FKS1 Hotspot 1/2 + bound ergosterol (8JZN), and DHODH explaining olorofim's >2,200-fold mold selectivity (1D3G); Martin Burke's extramembranous sterol sponge & kidney-safe AM-2-19, ReSTORE, FURI/CARES, FORMULA-OLS, OASIS, fosmanogepix FAST-IC/FORWARD-IM, voriconazole CYP2C19 TDM & fluoride periostitis, posaconazole 11β-HSD2 pseudo-hyperaldosteronism, and One-Health tebuconazole/ipflufenoquin stewardship

teenKit.tldr: Invasive fungi kill more people annually than tuberculosis and malaria combined, yet medical science has suffered a 20-year drought in developing new antifungal drugs—until now. By shrinking down to the atomic level, scientists are finally designing next-generation weapons to pierce fungal defenses.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Because fungi share core cellular machinery with human cells, fighting them without poisoning patients is one of modern medicine's hardest chemical balancing acts—and climate change is actively breeding deadlier, drug-resistant super-fungi right in our environment.
keyTakeaways: Fungal infections kill roughly 2.55 million people every year, a staggering death toll that dwarfs public health estimates from previous decades.
Single-letter mutations in fungal proteins—like swapping a single amino acid—can completely collapse the effectiveness of legacy drugs by destroying crucial water-bridges.
A massive 20-year drug development drought has finally broken with first-in-class therapies like rezafungin, olorofim, and fosmanogepix attacking fungi via entirely novel atomic pathways.

vocab.meaning: An emerging, drug-resistant super-yeast spreading rapidly through hospitals worldwide that evades standard disinfectants and legacy antifungal drugs.
The vital structural molecule found in fungal cell membranes that acts similarly to cholesterol in human cells and serves as a primary target for antifungal drugs.
The integrated framework recognizing that human health, animal health, and environmental ecosystems—such as agricultural pesticide use—are deeply and dangerously connected.
A cutting-edge imaging technology that flash-freezes biological molecules to capture their hyper-detailed, 3D atomic structures at an Angstrom scale.

quiz.question: How do invasive fungal deaths compare globally with major infectious diseases like tuberculosis and malaria?
options: Fungi cause significantly fewer deaths than either condition.
Fungi claim more lives annually than tuberculosis and malaria combined.
Fungal deaths are statistically negligible compared to viral pandemics.
Malaria still kills triple the number of people that fungi do.
quiz.explanation: Recent epidemiological data reveals invasive fungi account for roughly 2.55 million deaths a year, outpacing both tuberculosis and malaria combined.

quiz.question: Why is developing new antifungal medications chemically difficult for pharmacologists?
options: Fungi have hard outer shells made of pure diamond.
Fungi share eukaryotic cell structures and machinery with humans, making selective toxicity hard to achieve.
Fungal cells do not contain any proteins or DNA.
Fungi live exclusively inside deep-sea hydrothermal vents.
quiz.explanation: Because humans and fungi are both eukaryotes, drugs that disrupt fungal cell mechanics risk accidentally harming human cells too.

quiz.question: What agricultural practice has accidentally accelerated the rise of drug-resistant strains like Aspergillus fumigatus?
options: Using massive amounts of copper wire fences
Over-relying on agricultural azole fungicides like tebuconazole on crops like tulip bulbs
Sprinkling table salt over grain silos
Using ultraviolet light on wheat fields
quiz.explanation: Agricultural azoles select for resistant fungal mutations in the environment that eventually cross over to infect humans in clinical settings.
